title: Registry proxy + install bundle plan (TF notes)
body:
Purpose:
This is a working/playbook draft capturing a pragmatic approach for delivering an installable artifact bundle + a lightweight registry-proxy for customers that operate in isolated/air‑gapped VPCs or on‑prem environments. Goals: reproducible installs, safe upgrades, small blast radius, and Terraform-friendly interfaces we can hand to customers or embed in our on‑prem installer.

Summary of approach (high level):
- Provide a signed, versioned install bundle (tgz/zip) that contains: pre-pulled OCI images (or manifests), Helm charts, Kubernetes CRDs, operator binaries, and an artifacts manifest (checksums + signatures).
- Provide a small registry-proxy (containerized) that can be deployed in customer network to act as the local pull mirror for Kubernetes nodes / air-gapped clusters. The proxy supports: image rewrite, tokenless read from the bundle, and on-demand sync from an operator when connectivity to a staging sync host is available.
- Expose a Terraform module (inputs/outputs) for: creating the proxy deployment, mounting the bundle, configuring DNS/hosts rewrites, and producing a stable image prefix customers use in their manifests.
- Provide an upgrade plan for safe rollouts when a new bundle is delivered (signed delta bundles + validation hooks).

Key constraints we must respect:
- Customers vary widely in available disk/bandwidth — bundle must be modular so they can opt to exclude optional components.
- Idempotency and offline verification are critical — everything must include SHA256 and signature file (GPG or sigstore).
- Minimal attack surface — avoid long-lived external credentials inside bundles. Use short-lived bootstrap tokens for controlled initial syncs.

Concrete bundle layout (recommended):
- bundle-v{semver}/
  - metadata.yaml (version, release-date, components list, checksums, signed)
  - images/ (OCI tarballs, compressed) or manifest files (oci-layout + blobs)
  - helm/ (tarred charts, values-templates)
  - operators/ (binaries or containerized operator tarballs)
  - packages/ (apt/rpm repos tarballs OR package lists + checksums)
  - scripts/ (install helper: image-loader, mount-checks)
  - manifests/ (k8s manifests with image placeholders)
  - signatures/ (bundle.sig, metadata.sig)

Notes on images: prefer OCI tarballs generated via 'crane export' or 'oras' so that registries can either load them locally or the proxy can serve them. Provide both full-image tarballs for <small clusters> and manifest-only variants for customers who will pull from upstream via a proxy sync.

Registry proxy patterns (options):
1) Static file server + skopeo/crane loader: simplest. Host images as tarballs; nodes use a local registry cache (like registry:2) with files loaded via kube jobs. Pros: simple, firewall-friendly. Cons: slower first boot, needs node-level loader.
2) OCI registry (Harbor/Nexus) seeded from bundle: more featureful (auth, retention) but heavier. Provide a pre‑packaged container image + Helm chart.
3) Lightweight HTTP proxy with on‑demand regsync: proxy accepts upstream requests, if missing it attempts to fetch from an approved staging endpoint when connectivity exists. For strict air‑gap, proxy serves only pre-seeded blobs.

Terraform module notes (interface sketch):
Module name: redwood/private-registry-proxy
Inputs (examples - minimal set):
- name_prefix (string) - used for all k8s resources
- namespace (string)
- bundle_path (string) - path to mounted bundle inside cluster (e.g. /opt/redwood/bundle-v1.2.0)
- proxy_image (string) - image for proxy server
- storage_size_gb (number) - PV size for registry cache
- enable_helm_seeding (bool)
- allowed_components (list) - which subcomponents to seed (api, model-cache, examples)
- ca_cert_secret (string) - optional customer CA secret to inject for TLS termination
Outputs:
- proxy_endpoint (string) - host:port for cluster-local pulls
- seeded_images (list) - list of images successfully seeded (from manifest)
- bundle_checksum (string) - SHA256 of metadata.yaml for verification

Important TF design choices: keep module outputs deterministic and idempotent. Avoid encoding bundle contents into state; instead record just checksums and provenance (bundle URL, signed id). Provide lifecycle hooks for forcing re-sync when bundle checksum changes.

Sync & validation strategy:
- Preflight: validate bundle signature and checksums locally before any write. Abort if mismatches.
- Dry-run sync: module can run a dry-run mode to enumerate images that would be imported. Produce a "seed-plan" file that operators can review.
- Controlled seed: run a job (K8s CronJob or Terraform null_resource) that imports images into registry (or extracts tarballs). Record successes/failures to a log object (ConfigMap).
- Post-seed validation: pull test images on a couple of nodes, run smoke container to check that image loads and starts. Report latencies for largest images (for capacity planning).

Upgrade plan (high level):
1) Release bundle vN (signed). Publish only to staging site we control; notify customer with bundle checksum and release notes.
2) Customer reviews diffs (seed-plan) and schedules maintenance window.
3) TF plan: change bundle_path or bump bundle checksum variable => module triggers re-seed.
4) Seed in namespace isolated from production first (canary namespace). Deploy canary workloads using new images.
5) Smoke tests and regression checks (automated) — if passing, promote seeding to prod namespace and update image tags / Kubernetes manifests via image prefix rewrite.
6) Rollback: module supports revert to previous bundle checksum and automated purge of newly imported tags (or mark them deprecated). Keep old images for 7 days by default to allow rollback.

Bandwidth & sizing guidance (rules of thumb):
- Estimate total compressed bundle size = sum(image compressed sizes) + 10% metadata. For a typical Dedicated customer with 3 medium models + console + operators expect 40–120GB.
- Provide a "lite" bundle: exclude large optional model shards; provide model-on-demand instructions.
- For low-bandwidth customers, recommend seed from physical media (USB drive) or rsync via dedicated staging host across a high-bandwidth transfer window.

Tools & recommended commands (practical):
- Create bundle: crane export, oras rpush --output, tar + zstd
- Verify: sha256sum, gpg --verify (or cosign/rekor sigstore flow)
- Seed: skopeo copy file://image.tar docker://local-registry:5000/repo/image:tag OR use registryctl job to load OCI layout
- Inspect: crane ls, skopeo inspect, crane digest
- Rewriting manifests: use 'ytt' or 'kustomize' to replace image prefixes at deploy time

Common pitfalls & troubleshooting (notes):
- Node disk fills during seeding: make PV size conservative and monitor. Add eviction rules for temp loaders.
- Mismatched architectures: ensure manifest includes correct amd64/arm64 images or provide separate bundles per arch.
- Certificate issues: provide clear docs for customers to inject internal CA into proxy; include scripts to create k8s TLS secrets.
- Partial seed left inconsistent state: design a seed-plan with a state file — avoid destructive deletes unless explicitly requested.

Open questions / TODOs (short list):
- Decide default signing mechanism: GPG v. cosign (sigstore) — prefer sigstore for modern flow but need offline attestation story.
- Binary size vs convenience tradeoff for proxy image: keep <200MB if possible.
- Define retention / cleanup policy for old bundles in registry.
- Add terraform acceptance tests that run in CI against a minikube / Kind environment that mounts a sample bundle.

Immediate next steps (for this doc):
- Capture customer bandwidth/size targets from Solutions Eng (Marco).
- Prototype TF module skeleton (inputs/outputs above) and push to experimental repo.
- Build a minimal bundle (charts + 2 small images) and run end-to-end seed + smoke in Kind.

Appendix: quick checklist for on‑site handoff
- Provide signed bundle + checksum + bundle manifest
- Provide short runbook: mount bundle, validate signature, run seed-job, verify smoke tests
- Provide Terraform module with example usage and variables.tf commented sample
- Provide emergency rollback steps and contact info for SRE/SE on-call

End of draft — this is intentionally rough. Use as working blueprint for the more formal runbook and the TF module API we ship to customers.
